2. Respondent No.1 filed Miscellaneous Case No.123 of 1973 in the court of Munsif, Sherpur for correction of record of right under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It relates to land measuring 1.12 acres out of 2.00 acres of C.S. Khatian 1465 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No. 1760 and 13 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.1669 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No.2190 under Mouza Sherpur, District Mymensingh now Jamalpur. 

 3. In view of the point taken before us upon which leave has been granted, it is not necessary, I think, to refer to the facts stated in the petition. The case was contested by the predecessor-in-interest of the appellants. The trial court dismissed the aforesaid miscellaneous case on contest against the appellants and exparte against the rest. Respondent No.1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.115 of 1977 in the 5th court of Additional District Judge, Mymensingh against the trial court's judgment. On appeal the Additional District Judge set aside the judgment of the trial court. Being aggrieved the appellants moved the High Court Division which affirmed the judgment of the first appellate court. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider whether in view of the omission of section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by Ordinance No. LXIV of 1975 during the pendency of the aforesaid miscellaneous case, the first appellate court as well as the High Court. Division had jurisdiction to give relief to the respondents under this section suo motu. Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides as follows: 

 5. There cannot be any doubt that the grant of any relief under the provisions of this section would depend on its existence at the time the relief is being sought and granted. It appears that the aforesaid Ordinance omitting the section from the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force in January, 1976. The judgment of the trial court was delivered on March 31, 1977. In so far as the judgment resulted in the dismissal of the miscellaneous case, be such dismissal on any ground whatsoever, it is not hit by the omission of section 143A from the statute concerned. But point is when did the proceeding, namely, miscellaneous case under section 143A was started. As appears from the record, it started in 1973 when section 143A was not omitted from the Act. 

 8. It is true that the court exercises jurisdiction only when empowered by an Act of the legislature, therefore, when it has been negatived by the legislature by or under a subsequent enactment the court's jurisdiction to pass any order under the repealed Act or provisions of an Act is nullified. The omission of section 143A from the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is equivalent to repeal. 

 10. For the reason stated above, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.
